An archived loop is read-only: Overview, Live, Results, Files and Chat (an agent answers from the record) still read it; the document, files, settings, ideas queue, starts and resets are refused until Unarchive (a plain confirm). A start then rebuilds the deleted scratch. The loop lists hide archived loops; their Archived chip shows them, each with its date, and a search or a link still finds them. Run clean-ups leave them alone; the integrity checks, compaction and journal format updates still include them.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Someone who may view the loop but not edit it reads the problem here: the configurator's steps beside the document as written, the chosen step's lines lit. Nothing can be saved or checked.

  • Configurator: the document in six steps, as the Loop crafter shows it. A save shows its diff first; what the form cannot express is kept as written, greyed at the end of the document beside each step (Copy and Download give it whole) and listed on Save. A check or measurement the loader refuses is outlined on its row, with why. Save counts the document as checked once Check passed on its files as they are, or a start on those files got going. Every step but Graph and Save is a few light cards of rows, as the Graph's panel below: a label, then its box or menu, a greyed value its default, a unit (s, MHz, %, a number's own) inside its box, and no hint under a field -- the line at the step's foot says what the setting pointed at or in focus does. Prompt is the name, language, what to make and the rules, then Files; Check & Measure a Checks card (the list, a row opened to set it, the critic set in Graph) and a Measurements card (the list, then how many finalists the last one takes); Objective how designs are compared, then the numbers, a goal's unit in its box. Extra's sections (Parts, Baseline, Parameters, Running, Resources, More) are cards that fold, each saying what is set while folded; one set away from its default, or at fault, opens. On the Graph, a box clicked opens its panel: the box's name and what it does, then a few light cards. Worker says who works it, the same rows wherever a worker is chosen (a box, its Critic, Choose's Tie-break, a Knowledge section, an AI search policy): the kinds -- off first where it may be off (the workbench digest too), then agent, then the box's own (rules, mined, script, files, goals) -- then with agent an Agent menu, FluxAgent first, then the server's agents, then its Thinking and effort; Search's How it picks (FluxAgent only) follows, and right under them, folded, the agent's own card, titled <agent> · options: Questions and at most, Wait, Time limit and last turn, May time out, Session, Probe and its runs -- the same rows in every place, a row the place cannot say greyed (FluxAgent's are all an agent's; turns past the time limit and the probe are Design's agent's; Design keeps one session per part), its help line saying why. A box with a worker and a critic reads as two such blocks. Switching to another kind or agent and back brings back what it had (an agent's own settings, FluxAgent's thinking). The box's own card follows (Design's Per pass, Search's Policy with the settings it searches -- an AI policy is who proposes the points, FluxAgent with its Thinking and effort, or an agent with its card), and Limits, folded (Design's prototype limits, Search's exploration and FluxAgent's tool turns, which are the whole loop's: always in Design's panel, elsewhere where FluxAgent works). Under a search over settings Design is off, a script or files; with a script or files making each point, all its kinds. Check, Measure, Choose and Record are one block saying who works them, linked to where their commands or goals are set; Knowledge is a card per section. A card folds, its values said beside its title while folded; a dot marks a value the document sets, a greyed one is the default, and the line at the panel's foot says what the setting pointed at or in focus does.
  • Direct edit: the YAML as written, saved with its diff. A document that does not load is said before it is saved.
  • Agent: say what should change; an agent revises a copy of the loop's files and shows its diff (not while the loop runs).
  • Check runs flux task check on the document as it stands: whether it is ready to run, what it refused or found missing, then its checks, stages, objectives, tools and model. The whole output is under Details.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text: Groups, in the top bar between Loops and Admin, is every user's page for the teams they are in: who is in each group, what their membership gives them, whose settings their runs use, and the group's projects. Admins set groups up under Admin › Users › Groups (Server and admin); this page is where everyone else sees them.

docs.title: A tab per group
docs.text:
The page has a tab for each of your groups and one for Global (with its number of projects), with no title above them (the bar says Groups). The tab you chose is in the address (#/groups/<id>, #/groups/global) and remembered in this browser; a project opens under its group's tab (A project's page).

Under a group's tab:

Part What it shows Projects The group's projects: title and about, address (<group>/<name>), invite only or open · level beside the title, and your level on it -- what the project gives you (Viewer, Asker, Contributor, Lead; Custom only for a mix of boxes), with your group's curate or manage said beside it ("Asker + curate"); its words on hover; "—" when you only see it. An invite-only project you are not added to is not listed. The address is one line, cut with an ellipsis when it is long (the whole on hover). Members who may create, and admins, get the New project form under the list You in group A few facts: your Level (its words on hover, the words), what it Gives in plain words (curate or manage every project of the group, create projects; loops only through the projects you are in or that open to the group), Open projects (the level they give, for its managers and admins to choose) and Credentials in one line (the server's settings through it, through another group, or your own) Members · N Who is in it: names and levels for everyone; the member grid (a box per word) for whoever manages the group

On a phone You in comes first, then the projects and the members.

docs.title: Members
docs.text: A membership's level is Member, Maintainer (curate, create) or Lead (curate, manage, create): a group membership has no loop word. Being in a group gives nothing on any loop: a loop is reached when its owner shares it, or links it into a project you are in (or that opens to the group). A member who manages the group (a Lead) sees the members in the member grid, adds people with + Add people (they join as Member), removes anyone but themselves with ×, and gives levels and words up to their own; admins any. A member who may not manage the group sees the other members, their names and levels, read-only (never the words' table), and is told whom to ask. Nobody leaves a group from here.

docs.title: New project
docs.text: New project asks for a Title (free) and a Name, made from the title until you type one. The name is checked as you type: letters, digits, - and _, at most 60, and not one the group already has whatever its case. Create project makes <group>/<name>, blank and invite only, and you are its Lead (every word). Nothing is said under the form but an error, when there is one. A project's title opens its page.

docs.title: A project's page
docs.text:
Think of a group as an organisation and a project as one of its repositories, with members of its own; loops are linked into it. Its page opens on the Groups page, under its group's tab (the tab lit; a global project under Global): #/groups/<group id>/<name>, #/groups/global/<name>. Every link Flux makes to it is this one. An old address, #/projects/<group>/<name>, still opens it (a link in an older notification, a bookmark) and is replaced by the new one.

Under the group tabs:

  • Projects › its title ▾ -- Projects goes back to the group's projects; ▾ lists the group's other projects you see, with their loops, and + New project for whoever may make one. A pick opens the other project on the same tab when it has it.
  • Its head: the title, what the group's members get (🔒 Invite only, Group views, Open; a global project Public or 🔒 Private; its sentence on hover), You: your level (its words on hover), its address with a copy button, its about. Leave, a quiet button there, for its own members.
  • Its tabs: Overview, Library, Knowledge and Settings (only for whoever may change something there -- a Contributor's holds the topics alone; a plain member or a Viewer has none), each its own address: …/<name>/library, …/<name>/knowledge, …/<name>/settings.
Overview What it shows Loops · N Each loop linked into it that you may see: owner / name, its state, when last active, and for your own its place in the loop's order of projects ("1st of its 3"). + Link one of my loops if you hold the link role (anyone on a global project that takes loops); × takes one of yours out (the loop stays). A global project lists only your own loops, every one to admins and its managers, with whether each learns from its runs. What linking gives is on the ⓘ People · N Its members, names and levels (their words on hover); Manage › opens Settings for whoever keeps them Library How many files it holds and their size; Open › Your access Your words, and how you have them in a line: as a member, through the group, everyone on a public global project (what they give on its loops on hover)

On a phone the Overview is one column, Loops first.

Words: view, ask, edit, run -- what a member may do with every loop linked into it -- then link (link one's own loops in), curate (review what is learnt, keep the library) and manage (title, members, access; rename, archive, delete). Each implies view. A global project's members hold only curate or manage (Member, Maintainer, Lead): its visibility gives view. Sharing a linked loop stays its owner's. Words only add up: a project never takes one away.

Who manages it: its managers, the group's managers (manage on the group) and admins, each giving words up to their own. They also set what the group's members get -- Invite only (private: hidden until you're added -- only its members, the group's curators and managers and admins see it; a new project's default), Group views (they view it and its loops) or Open to the group (every member gets its Level for open: the group's default, or one of its own -- Viewer, Asker, Contributor or Maintainer -- that level, nothing more). There is no joining; anyone may leave a project. Others see its people, names and levels, in the Overview.

docs.title: Library
docs.text:
A project's Library is a folder of papers, specs and notes for its loops, browsed exactly as a loop's Files tab: the tree, the viewer (text in the editor, anything else to download), Add files and Add folder (or a drop; a single .zip is unpacked) into the folder open in the viewer, and Rename…, Move…, Delete… on the selected item. Its use is shown beside the room it has: a loop's, 100,000 files and 8 GB. Above it, which loops read it: every loop linked into the project reads it, read-only, at library/<name>@<group>/ of its own library (library/<name>@_/ for a global project), whoever runs it -- the loops you see are named, the others counted. An archived project's library is read by no loop, nor by a loop whose owner no longer views the project.

Who May Whoever views the project (its members, its group as its access says, everyone for a global one) browse and download edit, curate or manage on it -- as its member, through its group (an open project's level; a membership's curate and manage reach every project of the group), a global project's members with curate or manage upload, rename, move, delete, edit a text file manage (its managers, the group's managers, admins) Hide from AI / Show to AI: the paths the agents of its loops will not see (under its place, library/<name>@<group>/drafts/)

An archived project's library is read-only. Uploads, renames, moves, edits, deletes and hidden paths are on the audit trail.

docs.title: Knowledge
docs.text:
A project's Knowledge is what its loops have taught: short entries, each one insight, filed under the project's topics and proven by designs -- results of loops, never a number typed in. The accepted entries reach the project's loops at their next start: their agents query them with flux knowledge (list, search "<words>", show <id>; see Knowledge), and a coding agent's brief says so in one line -- the project's place and its topics with their counts. Proposals, rejected and retired entries never reach a loop; a run reads the entries as its start saw them, and its log line says the version ("project knowledge silicon@hw-lab 3f2a… (5 entries)"). People add entries by hand, and the collector proposes them from the loops' best designs (below).

The tab is a row of chips and one list. All and a chip per topic (with its count; the topic's question on hover) filter the list; To review, for its curators, holds the proposals; + Add is at the row's end. A row is an entry's headline with two muted lines of its analysis, its topic and how many designs back it at the right -- "✓ maria · 2 designs" when a curator ticked it, "+1" when it was reinforced today. A click opens it: the analysis at a reading width (a design named #142 in it is a link), its Designs (each a link to that design in its loop's Results, with its rank then -- "top 1 of 61" --, the day, how it came: "added by cy", "collected from nlu-gelu", later "from bob's chat in nlu-gelu"; one added later marked "+ … reinforced"), who accepted it, and Reinforce…, Edit and Retire for whoever may.

Who May Whoever views the project read the list; their own proposals, marked in review edit, curate or manage + Add an entry -- a topic, the insight in one line, the analysis (why it works, what the top designs did differently, citing them as #142, the cost, where it does not hold, what is open) and at least one design of a loop of the project they view; Reinforce… an entry in the list with another design, at once, no review; write the Topics curate (its curators, the group's curators and managers through the cascade) To review: open a proposal to change its headline and analysis, ✓ accepts it, ✕ rejects it; Edit and Retire an entry in the list

An entry's proof is enough with designs from 2 different loops. Until then it is a proposal; a curator's ✓ on one with less accepts it and ticks it ("✓ maria"), and the list says so. A curator's own entry goes straight in (ticked when its proof is short) -- on a global project another curator accepts it. A proposal may be marked contradicts: an entry's headline. Accepted, rejected and retired entries stay on the record; the author is told when a curator decides. An archived project's knowledge is read-only. Every change (topics, add, accept, reject, edit, retire, reinforce, a collector's run) is on the audit trail.

docs.title: The collector
docs.text:
Flux reads a loop's best designs for each project it is linked into -- unarchived, with topics, the link's learning on (on by default in a group's project; in a global one only its managers or an admin turn it on, and the loop's owner may turn it off) -- and writes what they teach as proposals, outside the loop: no step of the loop, nothing in its prompts or its folders changes. It looks once the loop's top 5 designs (by the loop's own ranking, as "top 1 of 61" says it) hold more than 3 that it has not read for that project: the loop's front has mostly moved since the last look. A design is read once; a name given again by a later start is another design. The server looks when a start ends and, while loops run, every two minutes at the ones whose record changed, one look at a time in the background.

A look is one call to the loop's own model -- its owner's FluxAgent settings for that loop, at their cost, about 6-12k tokens in and 3k at most out -- with the new top designs (their idea, their text or its diff against the loop's baseline, their numbers), the rest of the loop to compare, and the project's entries. It answers with at most six items, each checked before anything is written:

It finds What happens The new designs work by an accepted entry's mechanism They reinforce it at once, no review: "+ … collected from nlu-gelu, reinforced" A new insight A proposal in To review, "collected from nlu-gelu" They contradict an entry A proposal marked contradicts: its headline An entry is superseded or shown wrong A proposal retire: its headline, with the reason: ✓ retires the entry, ✕ keeps it. Nothing is retired by itself

Its rules are Flux's own: an insight answers a topic's question, in a one-line headline and an analysis of 80-200 words -- the mechanism, what the top designs did differently from the rest (citing them, #142), the cost, where it does not hold, what is open -- proven by the designs it names; no bare conclusions, vague tips or flag trivia, and nothing when the designs do not explain the mechanism and its limits. An item that does not hold (a topic or an entry that is not there, a design it was not shown, an analysis of the wrong length or citing none of its designs) is dropped and said on the audit. A call that fails reads nothing (the designs wait for a later look, not within the hour); a reply that is not the JSON asked counts as read. Curators see its last run in a quiet line under the list: Last collected: nlu-gelu · Oct 23 · 2 proposed, 1 reinforced (on hover: how many designs it read, how many items it dropped). Its calls count in Admin › Insights' usage as the loop's and its owner's, as knowledge collector under By agent (priced by the loop's FluxAgent token prices), and a failed one as a failed turn of its endpoint.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: For its managers (and admins): Members & access first -- its members in the same grid as a group's: a level (the words), the Member mark, a box per word, ×; All members gives or takes a word from everyone; + Add people (they join as Member); and what the group's members get, with the Level for open. Then About (title and about), Name with Rename… -- the new name is checked as typed, the old address stops working (no redirect) and its members and its group's are told the new one; the page opens at the new address -- Archive… / Unarchive and Delete… (type its name; its loops stay, taken out of it). On a global project admins also choose its Visibility -- Public (everyone sees it, its library and knowledge) or Private (only its members and admins) -- and who links loops into it (everyone, or admins only; a private one's members only). Topics, for whoever may edit the project (a Contributor too, who sees only this card): a row a topic -- its id (lower-case letters, digits, - and _) and the question its entries answer -- edited in place, + Topic, ✕, Save; YAML shows the project's knowledge.yaml as written (pipelining: Where do pipeline stages pay off, and what do they cost?, a line a topic, comments kept). A topic renamed takes its entries with it; one that still holds an entry is not removed. A member who may change nothing there (a plain member) sees no Settings tab.

docs.title: Global
docs.text: Global lists the global projects you see: the public ones (everyone sees them, their library and knowledge) and the private ones you are a member of (nobody else but admins finds them). Their members curate or manage them; there is no curator group. Only admins make them: New global project under the list (admins only), Admin › Users › Projects, or flux project create _/<name> (public; --visibility private). Anyone may link a loop into a public one, a private one's members into it (admins only when its join rule says so); it gives nobody any right on the loop, shows you only your own loops in it (admins and its managers see every one; in a private one its members do not see each other either), and learns from a loop's runs only once an admin or one of its managers turns that on.

docs.title: In no group
docs.text: A user in no group sees what a group is, that an admin adds them to one, and the Global tab. Their own loops and those shared with them are under Loops as always.

docs.title: Admins
docs.text: An admin sees their own groups; Every group (admin), at the end of the tabs, adds the others, marked "not a member". In every group an admin sets any member's level in the grid, the group's Credentials (Server settings or Own settings) and its open level, adds and removes members, and makes projects. Every group in Admin › Groups opens Admin › Users › Groups.

docs.title: Live
docs.text: A loop's Live tab shows what its run does, task by task, as it happens, and what earlier starts did. It has four views: Tree, Graph, Timeline and Log.

docs.title: The toolbar
docs.text:
• Start picks the start to show: the one running, or an older one, which replays its passes, tools and conversations.
  • Pass shows the current pass, all passes, or one pass (pass 0 is the baseline). Picking a pass that is over stops following.
  • Follow keeps the newest task in view; selecting a task pins it, and Following resumes.
  • Earlier passes loads passes before the most recent ones on a long run.

docs.title: Tree
docs.text: One line per task, tinted by its box and named by it (Search · arch=ripple, Check · golden), with a spinner while it runs. The steps every pass starts with fold into a Setup line, and finished passes fold; a folded pass says what it came to, the design it measured and its goal's number, ★ when it chose it (Pass 3 #3 · time_ms 155.6 ★). A design's tries read as they ran, the latest five, the earlier ones folded on top (▸ 31 earlier tries). The head is one line: the pass, then its counts -- its tasks (grey), done, failed, retried -- each count's word in its tooltip. A measurement says its design's numbers for the goals (confirm #6 · fmax_mhz 2543 · area_um2 5.074), the rest in the inspector. In the pass at work the boxes still to come are listed as waiting; a pass that ended on a failure lists the boxes after it as "not run". A pass's line opens the pass in the inspector: what it tried, where its time went, its boxes (Check · 5 checks ×3); every box row, a part of the time bar and what it tried open theirs (by click, Enter or Space), and a box's ‹ Pass 3 goes back.

docs.title: Graph
docs.text: The pass as the loop's drawing: Search, Design, Check, Measure, Choose, and a critic where one is set. Each box says what it is set to (Search what it picked), whether it passed (✓ or ✗), and ×N when it ran again; a design of several tries has a bar per try, ✓, ! (not built) or ✗. Boxes the loop skipped are dashed. With All passes, the chain of passes above the chosen pass's flow, and which pass it is (Pass 4 shown). A step bar fills once its step is done; one at work pulses, light. A Check or Measure box has a bar per step, not per run: five checks run three times are five bars, one stage measured ten times is one; a bar's tooltip sums its runs (check unit: 9 of 11 passed, 1 failed, 1 running), amber when it failed on the way, and a click opens its latest run.

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text: The start's time in lanes by box, passes as numbered bands, each try its own bar (its draft and its check); a Search that only picked its point is a tick in its lane. All passes takes the page's width, the inspector under it; many passes scroll sideways, the lane names kept in view. Passes (or parts) running at once each get a line of their own in a lane, the same line in every lane so a pass reads as one band, and share one numbered band ("1–3"); hovering a line names its passes; a run one pass at a time keeps one line per lane. A check or a measurement the agent ran itself in its try (flux probe) is a short tick in the Check or Measure lane at its own time, outlined in the agent's pink; its tooltip says the step, how it ended, its try and its time, and a click opens it. Per box: how many calls, the average, the longest, the total, and its share of the wall clock.

docs.title: Log
docs.text: The loop's log, numbered from 1 in the start shown, problems highlighted, each start and pass marked; on a phone a line's time is the time of day only. Follow it as it grows (it pauses when you scroll up), filter by text or /regex/, show only problems, or download it.

docs.title: The inspector
docs.text: Selecting a task opens it beside the list. A tool's task shows its command, folder, exit and time, and its output as it runs. An agent's task shows its reply, then its conversation: text, thinking and tool calls, each input and output. A model's try reads the same way: its prompt, the tools it called (a compute call's code and output, an ideas call as "proposed: "), then its reply in parts (why, the idea, the design as code, each edit as a diff) and its tokens. Paths under the turn's folder are shown relative to it. A prompt shows its input while it runs. <strong>Raw</strong> and <strong>Fullscreen</strong> open the whole of it.</p> <p>Under its title a task says where it is, the whole path: <code>Pass 2 › Design › try 8</code>, a tool call <code>… › try 8 › call 6</code>. A try that failed or was not built says why in a line under that. A box shows its runs with their state and time, its total time in its head; a box still to come says what the document sets it to, in a few words, with the YAML folded under them. A pass shows what it measured last and whether that was kept, where its time went (in the bar's order) and its six boxes, each with how many times it worked ("Design · 3 tries · 2 not built"); once it is over, a box it never reached says "not run", and a failed pass says why. A check's failures read "14 of 18 fail".</p> <h2 id="older-runs">Older runs<a class="headerlink" href="#older-runs" title="Permanent link">¶</a></h2> <p>A loop written by an earlier Flux keeps a task journal of an earlier form. Bring it up to date once with <code>flux task migrate FOLDER --journal EVENTS</code>, or on a server with <strong>Admin › Maintenance › Bring task journals up to date</strong>. Until then, Live shows its tasks as one setup pass.</p>

docs.title: Results
docs.text: A loop's Results tab holds every design measured across all its starts. The decision is said in a line above three views: Designs, Graphs and Ideas. The library's digests are under Files › Library (an old link to Results › Library leads there).

docs.title: Designs
docs.text:
One card of the designs, in four tabs, each with its count:

  • All: the accepted and the failed, the decision first. A design only its checks judged is a row too, blank in the measurement columns.
  • Accepted: the designs measured and accepted by the limits at their deepest stage.
  • Failed: refused by a check, a measurement that gave nothing, a limit missed, or rejected. No measurement columns: each check it went through (a pill each), the failure reason, when.
  • Pending: designs waiting for a stage: checked and not measured yet ("its pass ended before a stage measured it", "not measured yet: its pass is still running", "the run stopped before a stage measured it"), measured but short of the stage that judges them (their numbers so far), and those set aside to be measured again (re-measure pending, their old numbers muted).

Columns sort. Results opens on Accepted; the browser remembers the tab you choose; the address names it (…/results?tab=failed), and a link to a design opens it in its tab.

  • Absolute / Relative: numbers as they are, or as percent change from the latest baseline (without one, from the accepted designs' 90th or 10th percentile). Hover a cell for the value and its reference.
  • Numbers from an earlier stage: when stages measure different things (one timing, one area), a design's row shows each metric's deepest measurement; a number carried from an earlier stage is muted, and hovering it says which ("· from timing"). The design's detail writes that stage under the number.
  • Dictionary metrics: a dictionary's column is its own name; Tests ▸ unrolls its tests. A missing or empty test stays unmeasured, never zero.
  • Compare: tick two designs to see every number at every stage, the change (green where better), and their sources' difference.
  • A design opens with what it does not meet, its numbers at each stage, its idea and rationale, each check it went through (outcome, time, output; its pass opens in Live with each check's log), and its source; notes pinned on it from Chat, and Reference for comparison when it is marked so (for reading only: not the baseline the numbers compare with). The address names the open design (…/results?design=NAME): a link or a reload opens it.

docs.title: Checked, not measured
docs.text: A design only its checks judged opens the same detail as a measured one, with Not measured and why at its top: the check that refused it, a measurement tried that gave nothing ("its screen measurement was refused: estimated to fail"), or what it waits for. Check and measure again… (its owner, with a reason) has it checked and measured at every stage: by the running loop before its next pass, or at rest by a run of its own; it waits in Pending until then. flux loop show NAME says the same reason ("not measured: …").

docs.title: Reject a design
docs.text: Reject… on a design (its owner, with a reason) marks it: it stays shown but is never chosen. Tick its numbers to have them measured again or cleared; at rest, Also hide the design takes it out of the results, listed under Invalidated by hand, where Re-evaluate checks and measures those designs again in one run, and Restore counts them again. A critic's rejection reads the same way.

docs.title: Invalidate, re-evaluate, show hidden
docs.text:
After a check or a measurement script changed, the loop's Settings › Maintenance has three tasks for the record:

  • Invalidate all sets every design on record aside: each stays listed in Pending with its old numbers, marked re-measure pending and never chosen. Nothing is measured again yet: above the table (and on the Overview's designs tile) it reads "40 of 40 set aside since …: re-measure pending until a re-evaluation runs". Running it again adds only designs recorded since.

  • Re-Evaluate asks the loop's next start: after its baseline, that start checks and measures again the designs of Pending -- those waiting for a stage (checked, not measured) and those set aside (re-measure pending, Invalidate's included) -- then its passes go on. Its dialog has three boxes, each adding to what the next start measures again:

    • Rerun baseline: pass 0, first (a baseline on record otherwise stands).
    • Rerun failed: the designs of Failed -- refused by a check, measured to nothing, missing a limit, or refused by an earlier re-evaluation's checks; not those rejected by hand or by a critic.
    • Rerun all: every design on record, invalidated first (one rejected by hand too; its rejection stands). It ticks the other two.

Until that start the task's row and the Overview say what was asked ("the baseline measured again, then the pending designs re-evaluated") with Cancel; it can be asked while the loop runs. The pending or failed designs are written as one round when that start begins, each marked re-measure pending until measured. Each design's new numbers replace the old as it is measured: "re-measured 12 of 40 since the invalidation at …". A stop keeps every design measured so far: "paused: 12 of 40 done; continues at the next start" -- the next start measures only the designs still pending, the one a stop cut short included. A design today's checks refuse stays rejected, with why. - Show hidden evaluations is for records invalidated by an older Flux, where an invalidation hid every row up to it. The rows of designs never measured again since come back with their old numbers, set aside (re-measure pending) as Invalidate leaves them; the old rows of designs measured again since stay history (their new numbers stand), and designs invalidated by hand stay under Invalidated by hand. Its dialog says how many rows and designs it shows again. Nothing is deleted: the old mark stays on the record, beside the event that shows the rows again.

docs.title: Graphs
docs.text:
• Pareto front: any two metrics, by default at the stage the loop decides on: the designs it decides among (its pool) drawn and counted, every other design faint at the numbers it has, its point saying why it is not in the pool ("not a finalist on screen", "same design as …", a stage the document no longer has). Pool only hides the faint ones; picking a stage draws that stage's numbers instead. Accepted and failed coloured, the decision a diamond, the front joined. Focus fits the axes to the feasible front.
  • Improvement by design: the best so far for each metric chosen, design after design. Baselines are gray reference lines.

The choices (metrics, axes, stage, scope) are saved with the loop.

docs.title: Ideas
docs.text:
The loop's ideas notebook: each idea a model or agent proposed, and the trials that evaluated it. "Measured" means there is evidence, not that it improved anything; "refused" means every design that tested it was refused.

With the ideas cleanup on, an idea merged into another is folded under it ("merged into #3"), its evidence counted with the kept idea's, and the ideas it ranked come first, the most promising first, each with its reason; ideas proposed since come after them, newest first.

docs.title: Elsewhere
docs.text:
• Overview shows the decision against the limits, the best three designs, and a best-so-far chart. Its cards are chosen under Account › Overview layout.
  • flux report RECORD writes the same results as an HTML report beside the record.
